sources.news_title: Manhunt underway after off-duty Massachusetts police veteran found dead at woman's home
sources.text:
An urgent manhunt is underway in Massachusetts for a 58-year-old woman who police warn may be armed after a Worcester police officer was found dead at her home.
The Worcester Police Department said in an alert that officers are actively seeking Karen Solomon "regarding the death of a male at her residence."
Police described her as a 58-year-old White woman with dark brown hair and brown eyes last seen wearing pajama shorts and a tank top and walking toward Westcott Street.
NEW YORK STATE POLICE LAUNCH MANHUNT AFTER KILLING, HOUSE FIRE FOR 'ARMED AND DANGEROUS' SUSPECT
"There is concern she may be armed," the department said. Police have not publicly identified the man or said how he died.
Police said the officer found dead was a 30-year veteran of the force and was off duty at the time he was found. He has not yet been identified.
CBS Boston reported that Massachusetts State Police were searching the area with a helicopter and that a special emergency response team was being brought in to search nearby woods. Fox News has reached out to authorities for confirmation and additional details.
Solomon's home is on Wildwood Avenue, where authorities are conducting the death investigation, according to CBS Boston. The outlet also reported that Solomon said in a 2016 interview that she was married to a Worcester police officer and had made telling the stories of law enforcement a personal mission.
Solomon told WBZ-TV at the time that she was inspired to write "Hearts Beneath The Badge" after her son came home from school and asked why someone had told him that police "kill people for no reason." Solomon said she wanted to highlight the good deeds officers perform, from buying meals to saving lives and putting themselves in danger for others.
She later wrote "The Price They Pay," which focused on what she described as the darker side of policing, including the pain and anxiety officers can experience on the job.
Solomon also developed 1stHelp.Net, a website designed to connect first responders experiencing mental, physical or financial crises with resources. She told WBZ-TV that many officers she interviewed did not know where to seek help or were afraid to do so.
Neighbors told CBS Boston they were stunned by the developments. One resident described the officer as an "awesome guy" who he regularly saw walking around the neighborhood.

Police urged members of the public who spot Solomon not to approach her and to immediately contact authorities.
Anyone with information is asked to call the Worcester Police Department at 508-799-8606 or dial 911 in an emergency.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Worcester District Attorney's Office, Massachusetts State Police and Worcester Police Department for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

sources.news_title: Police seek Worcester woman in connection with death of a man at her home, officials say
sources.text:
Worcester police are searching for a 58-year-old woman who authorities say may be armed and dangerous after an off-duty Worcester police officer was found dead at a home Tuesday morning in what officials described as a domestic incident.
Police Chief Paul Saucier said officers responded to a home on Wildwood Avenue about 5:28 a.m. for a report of a person down and found a man dead, who was later determined to be an off-duty officer.
The officer, whose name was not immediately released, had served on the force for about 30 years as a patrol officer, Saucier said.
Authorities are searching for Karen Solomon, 58, who Saucier said “is presumed to be armed and dangerous.”
Worcester District Attorney Joseph Early Jr. described Solomon as a suspect and said investigators want to question her about what happened in the home.
“She was at the house,” Early said.
Officials said they could not discuss the relationship between Solomon and the officer, citing restrictions surrounding domestic violence cases.
Solomon is the founder and president of First H.E.L.P., an organization focused on reducing mental health stigma among first responders and raising awareness about suicide and mental health issues in the first responder community.
According to a biography on the organization’s website, Solomon is the author of “Hearts Beneath the Badge” and “The Price They Pay” and has written extensively about law enforcement suicide. Her work has focused on families who have lost officers to suicide and officers who feel they have nowhere to turn for help, according to the biography.
The biography says Solomon participated in a 2018 Officer Safety and Wellness Group Meeting, served as co-chair of the Data and Research Committee of the National Consortium on Law Enforcement Suicide Prevention and has served on an FBI task force involved in implementing the Law Enforcement Suicide Data Collection Act.
The biography also describes Solomon as the wife of a police officer.
Police said Solomon was last seen wearing pajama shorts and a tank top and was on foot walking toward Westcott Street.
Saucier urged anyone who sees Solomon not to approach her and instead contact police.
Local and state law enforcement officers are involved in the search, he said, as well as U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, and the U.S. Marshals Service.
Saucier said the FBI had also offered assistance if needed.
“We all come together and we try to make sure we have a resolution,” Saucier said.
Police were executing a search warrant at the Wildwood Avenue home as the search for Solomon continued.
Officials said that the investigation is in its early stages.
This developing story will be updated.
Bryan Hecht can be reached at bryan.hecht@globe.com. Follow him on Instagram @bhechtjournalism. Nick Stoico can be reached at nick.stoico@globe.com. Sean Cotter can be reached at sean.cotter@globe.com. Follow him @cotterreporter.

sources.news_title: Worcester police looking for woman who may be armed after male's death at her home
sources.text:
Police in Worcester, Massachusetts, are actively searching for a 58-year-old woman in connection with the death of an off-duty police officer, and investigators say they are considering her armed and dangerous.
Karen Solomon is described as having dark brown hair and brown eyes. She was last seen wearing pajama shorts and a tank top, walking towards Westcott Street.

Police shared a photo of Solomon to their Facebook page and said anyone who sees her should call 911 or the Worcester Police Department at 508-799-8606.
Worcester police said on Tuesday afternoon that the deceased man was an off-duty Worcester police officer. He was found after investigators were called to Wildwood Avenue around 5:30 a.m. Tusday.
Investigators have described the situation as a domestic incident. Officials would not confirm any relationship between Solomon and the victim, who was described as a 30-year veteran of the force.
